findings: The existing running-TCS rejection precedes the optional reserved-bit masking; ENABLE and other registers retain their rejection paths.
Only idle WAIT high bits use the explicit default-false reference policy. The low implemented sixteen bits are preserved and no command is triggered by this write.
The saturated diagnostic count retains its maximum and still records the latest voter/TCS/raw word. Later ordinary WAIT writes need not equal that historical last raw word.
Parent pre_load stops its timer, disables the input callback publish path through ready, and clears incoming subsection presence/policy and diagnostics.
The pinned VMState loader processes subsections before parent post_load. Profile presence/policy and diagnostic validity are checked before original output/timer restoration.
The optional subsection is present for every enabled profile including a cold zero-count instance. Missing/present mismatches reject both configuration directions.
Duplicate subsection and invalid subsection policy have explicit rejection paths. Diagnostics reject impossible zero-count last fields, unknown voter/TCS, and nonzero histories without ignored bits.
The main VMState v2 serialized fields and order remain unchanged. The new subsection serializes exactly 24 bytes excluding its subsection framing.
Reset clears diagnostics without modifying the immutable opt-in property. Existing resource validation and scheduling behavior remain in place.
conclusion: No static blocker found in this bounded C/header change.
scope_limits: No claim of silicon RAZ/WI behavior; the accepted masking is an explicit reference compatibility policy.
No compilation, QEMU, QTest, migration execution or public test was performed.
